messages.content: You translate German letters of the 1820s into plain modern English. Keep every fact, name, place, time and number. Add nothing, explain nothing, leave out nothing. Answer with the translation only.

Antwerp, 8 October 1822

My dearest Marie,

The journey has been vigorous. Van Ghert and I walked the fields of Waterloo for three hours, a landscape still heavy with the memory of that decisive blow to the old order. We then viewed the galleries in Brussels and the church of St. Gudula, before proceeding to Ghent. The academic handover there was tedious, but I endured it with the necessary dignity.

We departed Ghent by cabriolet at half past two, arriving here only after ten o’clock, exhausted by the long ride along the Scheldt. The city is bustling, the commercial spirit palpable. I am weary but content. Do not worry for me; I shall rest well and hope to continue northward soon.

Give my love to the boys. I think of you and our home in Berlin often.

Yours ever,
G. W. F. Hegel
